question: Does distinguishing observed positioning changes and their agreement with pre-existing price trend improve the following-quarter US broad-ETF return assessment beyond prices and positioning level?
user_authorization: Expand financial definitions and mechanisms, avoid high positioning automatically contrarian, assess increment professionally
decision_use: low-frequency trend participation research, no trades/position sizing; return use distinct from prior quarterly risk use
scope: US SPY, NAAIM and CFTC measured separately
literature definitions for crowding/flows/constraints, with China boundaries retained

proposed_definition.NAAIM_change: Mean_t - Mean_t-4 in percentage points; population aggregate, not same-manager trading
proposed_definition.CFTC_divisor_control: 100*(OI_t-OI_t-4)/OI_t-4 added to every price/control model, separately label baseline market activity
proposed_definition.trend: sign of prior252-observed-close SPY return; simple price state, not original LEI classifier
proposed_definition.lag_pair: t,t-1,t-2,t-3,t-4 consecutive source observations; total26-30days, each6-8days; exclude original2014NAAIM pair and all oldCFTC masks throughout interval; no interpolation

target.main: 100*(P_end/P_start-1),64 consecutive adjusted closes/63segments from next quote after hypothetical anchor; about1quarter
target.secondary: future maximum peak-to-trough drawdown only to describe forgone downside; not second optimized fit target
target.available_at: actual_release_at nullable remains unknown, uniform research alignment strictly after reportweekFriday, current-vintage exploratory only

target.endpoint: start=first quote after current anchor, end=start+63; anchor is first quote strictly after Friday of source reportweek

baseline: trend sign indicator; CFTC also denominator control

models.position: level + change only, not interpreted as strategy
models.context: change model + trend*change only; do not add trend*level

increment.primary: context relative to level: does the expanded definition help beyond current prices and position level?
decomposition: context vs change: trend conditioning representation
context vs prices and mean: stronger/simple opponents
increment.must_not_claim: combined improvement alone proves alignment/interaction; individual decomposition required

fit: fixed standardized ridge minimizes mean squared error+0.001 sum slope squared, intercept free; training-only mean/std; returns not clipped; yearly expanding2015-2026, only fully mature labels strictly before year start; all six models use identical source-specific eligible train/test rows, no outcome-based removal
description: four cells sign(trend252)*sign(change4w), zero change separate, show all groups and contiguous episodes, future return/risk and price residual; no cell renamed conviction/forced pressure; zero trend retained separately as well; episodes break on >8day source gap, removed rows or change of cell
uncertainty: paired26calendar-week blocks main,13sensitivity,2000resamples, retain calendar gaps and overlapping returns; report estimates and95%ranges, not hypothesis probabilities
robustness: leave each year using saved errors
